## Setup

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lme4) # probably a bit too optimistic with the amount of data we have!
```

## Background

I ran coding queries on PPCHY and our finished files, looking for pronominal/nominal object / reflexive / RP / RP-H preceding and following non-finite verbs in IP-MAT, IP-SUB, IP-INF and IP-PPL.

I have excluded cases where the element of interest precedes a finite auxiliary, as I'm assuming that these would not be informative.

### Summary of Variables

The messy version

| Variable | Labels | Comments |
| -------- | ------ | -------- |
| `ClauseType` | `mat`, `sub`, `inf`, `ppl` | IP-MAT, IP-SUB, IP-INF, IP-PPL, these are later sorted into Finite and NonFinite |
| `WordOrder` | `ov`, `vo`, `ovo`, `ovo_check` | "v" being the non-finite verb, "o" being a catch-all for object, reflexive, RP, RP-H. `ovo` is for cases where there is something relevant both preceding and following the non-finite verb, with `ovo_check` for the ones where the preverbal one is nominal (and the postverbal one might thus be of interest, based on the `Element` value. |
| `Element` | `rp`, `pronobj`, `rfl`, `posobj`, `qobj` etc | `rp` includes both RP and RP-H. There are additional `_and_` labels here that can be sorted according to the analysis, which include multiple elements of interest in the same toke. |
| `Modality` | `spoken`, `written` | I've switched from genre to this for now, as it's perhaps more relevant for our talk (and less messy). |
| `Year` | Numerical values | Based on ID labels (look out for confusion with token numbers though!) |
| `Corpus` | `ppchy`, `ourcorpus` | The files the data comes from. |
| `Text` |  | Whatever is printed in the ID labels |
| `Token` |  | Token label within the text, stripped off of ID label |

## Prepare Data

Load data, add variable names:

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
d1 <- read.delim("marjuqueries.ppchy.nodates.cod.ooo", header=F, sep=":")
d2 <- read.delim("marjuqueries.ourcorpus.nodates.cod.ooo", header=F, sep=":")

d <- rbind(d1, d2)
colnames(d) <- c("ClauseType", "WordOrder", "Element", "Modality", "Year", "Corpus", "Text", "Token")
head(d)
nrow(d)
```

Remove irrelevant instances with `z`:

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
data <- subset(d, ClauseType != "z" & WordOrder != "z" & Element != "z")

nrow(data)
```

Turn strings to factors, check:

```{r}
data <- mutate_if(data, is.character, as.factor)
data$Year <- as.numeric(as.character(data$Year))

summary(data)
```

Remove NAs (Some tokens without labels?)
```{r}
data <- na.omit(data)
summary(data)
```

Check for dating errors (when token number is listed as the year instead of actual year).

```{r}
data %>% filter (Year == Token)

```


Reorder some labels for convenience
```{r}
data$WordOrder <- factor(data$WordOrder, levels = c("vo", "ov", "ovo", "ovo_check"))

data$ClauseType <- factor(data$ClauseType,
                          levels = c("mat", "sub", "inf", "ppl"))
```

Combine IP-INF with IP-PPL and IP-MAT with IP-SUB for later plotting purposes
```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(Finiteness = ifelse(
    ClauseType %in% c("ppl", "inf"),
    "NonFinite",
    "Finite"
  ))
```


### Messy-messy!

The number of postverbal thingies in the different clause types:

```{r}
freq <- table(data$ClauseType, data$WordOrder)
freq
```

And percentages for each clause type:

```{r}
round(prop.table(freq, margin = 1) * 100, 3)
```

And a look at the different elements:

```{r}
table(data$ClauseType, data$WordOrder, data$Element)
```
#### Looking at the messy codes

Straightforward recoding:

* `ovo` for `posobj` is not behaving well and is picking up stuff where one of the nominal objects is before the finite verb. Recode these as `vo`. `ovo_check` ones would be true OVO for these, so I'll have to exclude them for now...
* `ovo` for `pronobj_and_posobj` means `ov` for `pronobj` and `vo` for `posobj`. Could double count these for the purposes of plotting to have more data in each category; likewise for `pronobj_and_qobj`
* `ovo` for `rfl_and_posobj` have `ov` for `rfl` and `vo` for `posobj`; likewise for `rfl_and_qobj`
* `rp_and_posobj` `ovo` are `ov` for `rp` and `vo` for `posobj`, vice versa for `ovo_check`; Same for `rp_and_qobj`.

Coding query things to worry about another time:

* `ovo` for `rp`, `rfl`, `rp_and_pronobj` and `rp_and_rfl` are a mess because they include cases with regular objects postverbally. Oops! Will need to fix the queries. For now, just exclude these hoping that I'm not generating a confound.
* just a couple of OVO ones for `qobj` - who knows what is happening here. Get rid. Maybe investigate later why these have different labels (these are from ourcorpus)
* currently no `posobj_and_qobj` label; worry about this later (if at all)

```{r}
summary(data)
```

## Exploring the Data

### Cleaner tables

Let's get the percent of postverbal occurrences for each element, in each clause type.
This will include clauses that have multiple such elements, and I'm just treating things on an individual basis here.
There are some exclusions as discussed in the messy bits above, some of which can be fixed by more thoughtful querying in the future

#### All data

```{r}
data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(RP, RFL, PRONOBJ, POSOBJ, QOBJ),
    names_to = "Constituent",
    values_to = "Order"
  ) %>%
  group_by(ClauseType, Constituent) %>%
  summarise(
    n_VO = sum(Order == "VO", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_OV = sum(Order == "OV", na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_VO = mean(Order == "VO", na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    result = sprintf("%.2f%% (%d/%d)",
                     prop_VO, n_VO, n_VO + n_OV),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  select(ClauseType, Constituent, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Constituent,
    values_from = result
  ) %>%
  select(ClauseType, RP, PRONOBJ, RFL, POSOBJ, QOBJ)  %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Proportion of VO order by IP type and constituent (all data)"
  )
```

### Make some plots

#### All data, by Clause Finiteness (instead of ClauseType), to simplify

TODO: This will need cleaning up
Probably want to highlight the non-finite clauses, so swap the line styles?

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(RP, RFL, PRONOBJ, POSOBJ, QOBJ),
    names_to = "Constituent",
    values_to = "Order"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Year, Constituent, Finiteness) %>%
  summarise(
    n_VO = sum(Order == "VO", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_OV = sum(Order == "OV", na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_VO = n_VO / (n_VO + n_OV),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Year,
    y = prop_VO,
    colour = Constituent,
    linetype = Finiteness,
    group = interaction(Constituent, Finiteness)
  )) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.4, se = F) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Proportion of VO",
    colour = "Constituent",
    linetype = "Finiteness"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
